criteria.error_taxonomy: Verify returns distinct domain failures for malformed, expired and wrong-session tokens so callers branch per cause.
criteria.false_all: Verify returns false for every failure including empty secrets, empty sessions and bad durations, collapsing config and token faults.
criteria.false_vs_config: Verify returns false for token faults (malformed, expired, wrong session or secret) and fails domain errors only for invalid configuration (empty secret, empty session, out-of-range durations).

csrf_failure.instructions: How should CSRF verification failures reach the caller?

criteria.all_pairs: Lookup returns every pair for the name in wire order and the caller selects; no positional default is blessed.
criteria.first_wins: Lookup returns the first pair for the name, matching the native get, while the full ordered pair list stays available for inspection.
criteria.last_wins: Lookup returns the last pair for the name, treating later pairs as overrides of earlier ones.

duplicates.instructions: Which pair should duplicate request-cookie lookup return?

criteria.adapter_enforces: The adapter rejects prefix violations (__Host- without Secure plus Path=/ and no Domain; __Secure- without Secure) and SameSite=None without Secure with domain errors before serializing.
criteria.enforce_prefix_only: The adapter enforces name-derived prefix rules but passes SameSite combinations through to native serialization.
criteria.serialize_native: The adapter serializes whatever the native constructor accepts and documents browser treatment; no adapter-side policy.

policy.instructions: Should the adapter enforce cookie prefix and SameSite rules?

criteria.default_secret: Callers may omit the secret and use the native thread-local default that changes at restart.
criteria.explicit_required: Every call takes a caller-supplied secret plus a nonempty session id; no defaults exist.
criteria.secret_handle: Secrets travel as opaque issued handles, never raw strings, mirroring the crypto key model.

state: Can compiles to TypeScript for pinned Bun 1.4.2 (bun-1.4.2-darwin-arm64-v1, revision 744846f844374847c902b5e7fd59b4342a51ef99). B1-09 adds typed cookies and session-bound CSRF over the B1-06 HTTP and B1-08 crypto contracts. Pinned probes observe: CookieMap keeps every duplicate pair in wire order while get returns the first (first-wins) and toJSON keeps the first; names are case-sensitive; segments without '=' and empty names drop; empty values stay as empty strings; surrounding spaces trim; quoted values do not unquote and split at inner semicolons; percent-encoded values percent-decode; split happens at the first '='; missing names get null and has false. Bun.Cookie defaults to Path=/ and SameSite=Lax and always emits both; SameSite=None without Secure serializes without the flag; bogus sameSite throws TypeError; names reject CRLF, semicolons, spaces, '=' and emptiness with TypeError while commas pass; values percent-encode (CRLF, semicolons, unicode); __Host- and __Secure- names serialize with any attributes (no prefix enforcement); negative maxAge serializes as-is; maxAge zero or past expiry reads expired. CookieMap deletion emits empty-value epoch-expiry fields carrying the requested domain and path; getSetCookie round-trips repeated fields while plain get comma-joins them. CSRF tokens are 86-character strings, distinct per generate; verify returns false for wrong session, wrong secret, garbage, truncated and bit-flipped tokens; session binding is strict both directions; empty sessionId, empty secret and non-string tokens throw TypeError; missing options verify false; the thread-local default secret self-verifies; token expiry is absolute over maxAge; maxAge zero still verifies fresh tokens while negative or huge maxAge and negative expiresIn throw RangeError. Filetree bounds hold: runtime/platform/cookies.ts and csrf.ts carry the adapters, http.ts keeps repeated Set-Cookie fields separate, one emit/runtime_cookies.go binds both modules. Adapters return the Completion representation with source origin and declared error boundaries. Assertions never compare whole random token strings; cookie transforms run real; session derivation and unsafe-request coverage stay application logic.
